title: 1978 AHSME Problem 4
statement: If \(a=1,\) \(b=10,\) \(c=100\) and \(d=1000,\) then \[ \begin{aligned} &(a+b+c-d)+(a+b-c+d)\\ &\quad+(a-b+c+d)\\ &\quad+(-a+b+c+d) \end{aligned} \] is equal to

solutions.text:
Each variable appears positively three times and negatively once, so the expression is \[ \begin{gathered} 2(a+b+c+d)\\ =2a+2b+2c+2d\\ =2+20+200+2000\\ =2222. \end{gathered} \]

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Count how many times each variable appears with each sign
The entire sum simplifies to twice \(a+b+c+d\)
